root_cause.text: The vulnerability is caused by the `amdgpu_pci_probe` function incorrectly modifying the global `amdgpu_aspm` variable based on the ASPM capability of a single PCI device, leading to inconsistent power management states and crashes in multi-GPU systems where devices have differing ASPM support.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the code block `if (amdgpu_aspm == -1 && !pcie_aspm_enabled(pdev)) amdgpu_aspm = 0;` from `drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_drv.c`, which the commit message explicitly states was erroneously applied and causes "very hard to debug crashes, when used with a system with two AMD GPUs of which only one supports ASPM."

vuln_statements.explanation: Based on the vulnerability root cause, this statement (or similar) in amdgpu_pci_probe incorrectly modifies the global amdgpu_aspm variable based on the ASPM capability of a single PCI device. In multi-GPU systems where devices have differing ASPM support, this leads to inconsistent power management states and crashes. The statement should instead consider all devices' ASPM capabilities before setting the global variable.
